_src.quote: These instructions all have names of the form V_MFMA_[output type]_[M]X[N]X[K][_[B]B]_[input type] where B

concepts.notes: Decoder for every mnemonic in v1's `instructions` array: e.g. V_MFMA_F32_32X32X1_2B_F32 is M=32, N=32, K=1, B=2, f32 in / f32 out; V_MFMA_F32_32X32X2_F32 has no _[B]B group so B=1. Worked example on the same page: V_MFMA_F32_32x32x1_2B_F32 performs D[0,:,:] = C[0,:,:] + A[0,:,:] * B[0,:,:] and D[1,:,:] = C[1,:,:] + A[1,:,:] * B[1,:,:]. concepts.statement: These instructions all have names of the form V_MFMA_[output type]_[M]X[N]X[K][_[B]B]_[input type] where B (which is 1 if not specified) is the number of matrices (or blocks) that are multiplied, and M, N, and K, are the multiplication dimensions for each block.

_src_extra.quote: respectively, of the ACC field of a MFMA instruction (0 for VGPRs, 1 for AccVGPRs), while the ACC_CD bit
determines if the C and D matrices are stored in VGPRs (0) or AccVGPRs (1). Data can be moved to and from
(VGPRs) or accumulation VGPRs (AccVGPRs), which are additional registers exclusive to the matrix core unit.

concepts.notes: THE register-file selection rule, and the highest-value fact on PDF p.50. Decoded per operand: ACC[0] (the low bit) selects the file for matrix A; ACC[1] (the high bit) selects the file for matrix B; the separate one-bit ACC_CD field selects the file for BOTH C and D together. In every case 0 = ArchVGPR, 1 = AccVGPR. Consequences a kernel author will act on: A and B can live in different files, but C and D cannot be split from each other. CAUTION -- the PDF sentence is grammatically broken as printed: "The register file that the registers holding matrices A and B are controlled by the low and high bits, respectively, of the ACC field" is missing a verb phrase (something like 'come from is'). The statement field above is the repaired reading; the verbatim text is in the _src quotes and in L.err.p50-register-file-sentence. The meaning is not in doubt -- only the grammar. Recorded at _conf verbatim for the mapping, because the (0 for VGPRs, 1 for AccVGPRs) and ACC_CD clauses are unambiguous as printed. The bit-position decoding of 'low and high bits' onto ACC[0]/ACC[1] is the only derived step.
concepts.statement: The input and output values for an MFMA can be stored either in the standard architectural vector registers (VGPRs) or accumulation VGPRs (AccVGPRs). The register file for the registers holding matrices A and B is controlled by the low and high bits, respectively, of the ACC field of a MFMA instruction (0 for VGPRs, 1 for AccVGPRs), while the ACC_CD bit determines if the C and D matrices are stored in VGPRs (0) or AccVGPRs (1).

_src.quote: Note that the registers holding input or output data for a MFMA instruction must be contiguous, and that the

_src_extra.quote: first register must be aligned to the number of registers required as the input or output. For instance, if an
instruction requires four input registers for matrix A, registers 4 through 7 may be used (by setting SRC0 to 4)

concepts.notes: The second highest-value fact on PDF p.50, and a hard constraint on register allocation. Two separate requirements: (1) CONTIGUITY -- the N registers of an operand must be consecutive; (2) ALIGNMENT -- the base register number must be a multiple of N, where N is the number of registers that operand requires. The PDF's own example is the whole proof: a 4-register A operand may start at 4 (4 % 4 == 0, giving v[4:7]) but not at 5 (5 % 4 != 0, so v[5:8] is illegal) -- so this is NOT merely even/odd alignment, it scales with the operand size. Note the PDF states the alignment as 'aligned to the number of registers required'; it does not say what happens for operand sizes that are not powers of two, and no MFMA in the v1 `instructions` array has one, so that case is untested by the spec. This rule covers both inputs and outputs ('input or output data'). v1 carries this sentence only as a trailing clause inside the notes field of layout_rules[notation.general], whose _src points at PDF p.55 (section 7.1.4) -- the sentence is actually printed on p.50 in the 7.1 preamble, so this record supplies its correct provenance.
concepts.statement: Note that the registers holding input or output data for a MFMA instruction must be contiguous, and that the first register must be aligned to the number of registers required as the input or output. For instance, if an instruction requires four input registers for matrix A, registers 4 through 7 may be used (by setting SRC0 to 4) but not registers 5 through 8.

concepts.notes: The axis convention for every layout table in chapter 7: COLUMN = lane, ROW = register (or logical item). Getting this backwards transposes every layout in the database. concepts.notes: The only fully worked example of the notation itself, and the template every later layout table follows. Witness cells transcribed from the p.50 table by eye: (reg 0, lane 0)=A[0,0,0]; (reg 0, lane 1)=A[0,1,0]; (reg 0, lane 31)=A[0,31,0]; (reg 0, lane 32)=A[1,0,0]; (reg 0, lane 63)=A[1,31,0]; (reg 1, lane 0)=A[0,0,1]; (reg 1, lane 1)=A[0,1,1]; (reg 1, lane 31)=A[0,31,1]; (reg 1, lane 32)=A[1,0,1]; (reg 1, lane 63)=A[1,31,1]. Reading: the LANE index walks the row index i (and the block at the 32-lane boundary), while the REGISTER index walks the column index j -- consistent with v1 layout_rules[dense.in.a] for M=32, B=2, K_L=2. The preceding storage-layout box on the same page contains a typo in its 5th data row -- see L.err.p50-notation-example-a-typo. This example is deliberately NOT filed in layout_rules: it is not tied to an opcode and v1's figure_layouts record shape (lanes/mn/vgprs/k cells) does not fit a Lane x Register value table.
concepts.statement: Worked notation example (section 7.1.1). Given two blocks of A written in storage layout (each block is 32 rows by 2 columns -- that shape is DERIVED from the box's own extent, the page never prints the dimensions), the corresponding register layout is: Register 0 holds A[0,0,0] A[0,1,0] ... A[0,31,0] in lanes 0..31 and A[1,0,0] ... A[1,31,0] in lanes 32..63; Register 1 holds A[0,0,1] A[0,1,1] ... A[0,31,1] in lanes 0..31 and A[1,0,1] ... A[1,31,1] in lanes 32..63. This means that each lane of a wavefront holds two values across two contiguous registers, which are the two values of a row of one of the blocks of A, with the first 32 lanes holding a different row from block 0 and the second 32 lanes holding successive rows of block 1.

concepts.notes: The stated RATIONALE for the b-dependent term in v1's general output lane formula j + N * ((i / H) % M_I + M_I * (b % B_I)): when M * N / H < 64 the leftover lanes are filled with successive blocks rather than left idle, which is exactly what B_I = ceil(64 / (N * M / H)) counts. v1 carries the sentence inside the notes string of a layout_rules[dense.out] example; recorded here for its own p.54 provenance because it is the only place the spec explains WHY B_I exists.
concepts.statement: That is, because there are not enough groups of 4 rows available in a block to fill 64 lanes of output in each register, successive blocks are used instead. Note that these outputs are 32-bit floats and so are not packed into registers.

_src.quote: from the previous section, each lane needs to hold four values. This is because each input register holds two

concepts.notes: The concrete, worked statement of v1's packing_rules[packing.16bit] ('odd-numbered items taking up bits 31-16 and the even ones in bits 0-15', PDF p.56). The two agree: the 'second' 16-bit value of a register is item 1 (odd) and sits in bits 31-16. Note the PDF writes the range as '(16-31)' here with an em/en dash and as '31-16' on p.56 -- same field, opposite bit order in the printed notation. Recorded for that provenance, not as a new packing rule.
concepts.statement: The instruction uses 2 registers to hold each of A and B, even though, following the input format principles from the previous section, each lane needs to hold four values. This is because each input register holds two half-precision values, with the second of those values in the upper bits (16-31) of the register.

verification.method: 5-way parallel extraction (split by section, each agent spot-checking its own output against re-rendered pages) + a merge agent running four tests; then a coverage audit binning every record against the PDF bookmark tree and caption census, and a gap-fill pass (fragments L, M) for the chapter-7 pages that audit showed uncited.
verification.standing_caveat: Every genuinely CDNA4-new surface -- the four F8F6F4 opcodes, E8M0 scaling, 6-bit packing, the K=128 shapes and the new sparse shapes -- has exactly ONE channel of evidence behind it, because no tool reaches them. The 11776-element cross-check covers only what CDNA4 inherits from CDNA3. Validate a low-precision layout numerically on hardware before trusting it in a kernel.
